headline: Tropical Storm Lala Batters Hawaii as Multi-Front Crisis Continues: US Heat, Colombia Quake, Midwest Floods, and Kilauea Eruption All Active
overview: August 20 sees an unusually broad convergence of natural hazards across multiple continents. Hawaii is emerging from a direct tropical storm strike — the remnants of Hurricane Lala — while the continental US simultaneously endures a weeks-long extreme heat emergency, catastrophic Midwest flooding now drawing federal disaster declarations, and severe thunderstorms spawning fresh flash floods from Missouri to Ohio. Globally, rescue teams in Colombia continue to work through rubble from last week's M7.4 earthquake, Kilauea's latest lava fountaining episode is underway on the Big Island, and European firefighters are battling both the Belgium High Fens blaze and deadly wildfires in Greece.

events.title: Tropical Storm Lala Strikes Hawaii — Flooding and Damage Persist
events.summary: Hurricane Lala made landfall on the Big Island before weakening to a tropical storm, bringing destructive winds and heavy rainfall that caused widespread flooding across Hawaii. Emergency responses remain ongoing as of August 20, with city facilities in Honolulu still operating in crisis mode and flood damage persisting across multiple islands. The storm marked a rare direct tropical cyclone hit on the Hawaiian island chain.

articles.title: Hurricane Lala weakens to a tropical storm, but flooding persists in Hawaii | Weather News | Al Jazeera

events.title: U.S. Extreme Heat Emergency Extends Into Third Week — 115°F+ in Death Valley, Phoenix Warnings Through Aug. 23
events.location: Arizona, Nevada, California, Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, USA
events.summary: Active Extreme Heat Warnings from the NWS cover a vast swath of the American Southwest, South, and Southern Plains on August 20, with temperatures reaching 115–118°F in the Death Valley and lower Colorado River Valley corridor and 108–112°F across the Phoenix metro area — warnings there now extended through August 23. North Texas faces highs to 108°F and Oklahoma heat indices to 110°F, while Southern California's Coachella Valley sees temperatures to 112°F. The NWS Las Vegas office notes this represents the longest sustained heat wave of 2026, posing a major HeatRisk to millions.

events.title: Colombia M7.4 Earthquake — Death Toll Climbs, Congressional Rescue Effort Ongoing
events.location: San José del Palmar, Chocó Department, Colombia
events.summary: Rescue operations continue following the devastating M7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia on August 10, with the death toll having surpassed 250 and thousands more displaced across Chocó Department. ReliefWeb situation reports through August 13 detail severe infrastructure damage, with remote communities still cut off by landslides triggered by the quake. Humanitarian organizations warn of compounding risks as access to clean water and shelter remains critically constrained.

events.title: Midwest–Ohio Valley Flooding Escalates — Federal Disaster Request, Wabash Warnings Through Aug. 29, New Flash Floods in Ohio and New Jersey
events.location: Indiana, Illinois, Ohio, Missouri, Kentucky, West Virginia, New Jersey, USA
events.summary: The ongoing Midwest flooding crisis has significantly escalated as of August 20, with the NWS extending Flood Warnings on the Wabash River at multiple gauges through as late as August 29, and congressional representatives formally urging the White House to approve a major federal disaster declaration for Indiana. Overnight, fresh rounds of severe thunderstorms dropped 2–4 inches of rain over central Indiana, western Kentucky, southeastern Missouri, and western Ohio, generating simultaneous Flash Flood Warnings across Preble, Greene, and Montgomery counties in Ohio and Hendricks, Morgan, and Putnam counties in Indiana. A new multi-day Flood Watch is active for portions of New Jersey, New York City, and northern Delaware ahead of additional heavy rainfall Thursday afternoon, broadening the impacted zone considerably beyond prior reports.

events.title: Kilauea Volcano — 53rd Lava Fountaining Episode Underway on Hawaii's Big Island
events.summary: Kilauea's summit eruption has entered its 53rd lava fountaining episode, with precursory activity beginning around August 12 and intermittent lava dome fountaining and overflows from the north vent ongoing. The eruption is confined to Halemaʻumaʻu crater within Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, posing no immediate threat to populated areas, though volcanic gas (vog) emissions are a concern for downwind communities. The episode coincides with the broader crisis brought by Tropical Storm Lala, compounding hazards on the Big Island.

events.title: Belgium High Fens Wildfire — Rains Aid Containment After Record-Breaking Blaze
events.location: High Fens (Hautes Fagnes) Nature Reserve, Belgium / German Border
events.summary: Rainfall has begun aiding containment efforts against the High Fens wildfire, Belgium's largest on record, after firefighters spent days attempting to 'definitively encircle' the blaze that scorched well over 3,000 hectares of protected peatland bog and pine forest. Crews had been supported by European aerial assets, and the defensive line protecting evacuated villages was reported to be holding as of August 18–19. While rains represent a notable positive development, conditions in the peat-rich High Fens — where fires can smolder underground — mean the threat is not fully extinguished.

articles.title: Belgium wildfire: Rains help High Fens containment efforts

events.title: Greece Wildfires — Deaths Confirmed on Salamina Island, Arson Arrests Near Athens
events.summary: At least two people have been killed by wildfires on the island of Salamina, west of Athens, as fires continue to burn across the Attica region in Greece. Authorities have made arson-related arrests on Salamina, with investigators pointing to deliberate ignition as a key driver of the outbreak. Firefighters remain stretched across multiple simultaneous fronts as hot, dry conditions persist across the Eastern Mediterranean.
